note: Malhun lives in long sung poems, live gatherings and Moroccan cassettes and broadcasts; no named malhun recording could be confirmed online yet, so there is no playlist.

size.basis: No catalogue counts malhun recordings. The Moroccan Ministry of Culture issued a 3-CD malhun set (mentioned in an M&A review of the 2001-2002 Anthologie de la Musique Marocaine); the genre's text corpus runs to many hundreds of qasidas by named poets from the 16th to 20th centuries (French Wikipedia lists dozens of poets and printed anthologies, e.g. Guessous 2008/2014). Recordings exist mainly as radio archives and cassettes by singers such as Houcine Toulali (1924-1998), so the issued-track range is a judgement. Core: a few dozen qasidas that every malhun audience knows (e.g. Chamaa, Herraz Aouicha), each recorded by several singers.
